subject: Post-Inference Alley: prioritization & next steps
body:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@convexa.ai>, Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Great to meet you at Inference Alley — quick follow-up

Hi Sanjay / Clara —

Really enjoyed our conversation at Inference Alley about Convexa's multi-model routing and latency spikes during peak batch windows. I promised to share a short recap and a suggested next step.

Quick notes from the booth chat:
- Primary use case: real-time inference for search-ranking reranker (90–200ms target P95).
- Current infra: self-hosted instances with mixed GPU types, occasional tail latency during holiday load tests.
- Top constraints: data residency for EU customers, and predictability for burst events (marketing campaigns).

Suggested next step: 30-minute discovery call where we map their traffic profile to a recommended Dedicated configuration and quantify likely cost delta (batching + KV cache + fallback to quantized variant). I can run a micro-benchmark with a small sample model if you can share a representative prompt set (anonymized).

Attachments: a one-pager on Redwood Dedicated and an outline of a minimal MPA (attached).

Are you available for a short call next week? I’ll include Marissa on the sync since she helps size Dedicated pools.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: redwood-inference-one-pager.pdf (1 page summary)
Attachment: convexa-mpa-outline.docx (proposal outline)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@convexa.ai>, Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery — Convexa / Redwood (notes)

Thanks for the call earlier — notes and next steps below.

Key takeaways:
- Traffic shape: 60% short text queries (<=64 tokens), 40% long-form ranking contexts (avg 256 tokens).
- SLO target: P95 <= 200ms for ranking path; burst headroom needed for Black Friday-like spikes.
- Compliance: EU data must remain in EU region for a subset of traffic.

Proposed phased approach:
1) Pilot: 2-week Dedicated pool (2x A100 equivalent) anchored in us-west for primary traffic, plus EU-sited fallback nodes for residency; run live traffic at 5–10% to measure latency profile (bench + live).
2) Cost estimate: we’ll share a modeled delta vs current fleet after we run a small micro-benchmark.
3) Security/compliance: Marissa will coordinate SOC2 artifact requests and a short questionnaire.

Action items:
- Sanjay: share two anonymized prompt files and recent 24-hour tail latency CSV (redacted) — due 11/20
- Diego: run the micro-benchmark and return modeled cost delta + a proposed pilot config — due 11/24
- Marissa: send SOC2 evidence checklist and Redwood onboarding doc — due 11/20

Attachments: inference-readiness-checklist.xlsx (template)

Cheers,
Diego

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Quick check — sample files & pilot timing?

Hey Sanjay —

Wanted to bump this thread. We didn’t see the sample files come through in the shared folder and I wanted to check whether Convexa still plans to run the pilot before the end of the year. If priorities shifted, totally understood — quick options:

1) Still on for pilot: please drop the sample prompts + CSV and we’ll schedule the micro-benchmark this week.
2) Need more time: tell us a better timing window and we’ll align the pilot start.
3) Not a priority: happy to pause and reconnect after your internal roadmap is stable.

I attached a one-pager and the pilot outline again for easy reference. If it helps, I can schedule a 15-min call to unblock this quickly.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
